dct_creator_sm: Castello, Pablo P. (Queen's University. Department of Philosophy).
dct_description_sm: This Appendix provides data in the form of videos, photographs, and a digitalised transcription of notebook notes and drawings, substantiating the empirical claims made in the article. The structure of the appendix mirrors the article’s structure, i.e., section 3.1 of the appendix compiles data that backs the empirical claims made in section 3.1 of the article, and the same applies to sections 3.2 and 3.3. Each section contains subheadings capturing an empirical claim made in the article (e.g., ‘Cows and turkeys cleaning other residents’), below each subheading there are images, videos, notes, and/or drawings substantiating the claim at stake. Underneath images, videos, and diagrams, I provide a description of what appears in the data. In the descriptions, I have sometimes written ‘note’ in order to indicate that that part of the text is a direct transcription from the notebooks. On how this data was collected, see section 2 of the article and the User’s Guide.
dct_rights_sm: Researchers who would like access to The Fabric of Zoodemocracy’s data must agree to the following stipulations: the data will be used only for research purposes; users may not copy the data (nor any part of it) nor make the data (or any part of it) available on any type of electronic network without the written permission of VINE sanctuary and the The Fabric of Zoodemocracy’s author, Pablo P. Castello. If permission is granted by the author and VINE, users will exercise due caution to prevent others from copying, distributing, or misusing the data. Researchers must agree to these conditions by filling out the form that is prompted when requesting access to the dataset. VINE requires explicit permission for the use of this dataset, as its ethos prioritizes placing animals' interests and voices at the centre of their decisions. Consequently, any request to use this data will be evaluated to determine whether the intended use aligns with VINE's ethical principles and values. Specifically, VINE members of staff consider whether VINE’s nonhuman residents, if hypothetically capable of understanding the purpose of the data’s use, would consent to the reproduction of photographs or videos of themselves for those purposes. We invite prospective users of the dataset to engage with VINE and the author in a transparent dialogue about the users' intended purposes, allowing us to make thoughtful and principled decisions regarding access and use.
dct_title_s: Appendix of The Fabric of Zoodemocracy
